questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Two men whose names are linked to painful parts of history
The most popular baby names around the world
How parents choose names for their children
Why many people in Britain change their names after marriage
questions.why: Beth says they'll meet two people whose family history made them consider changing their name.

questions.q: What point does Neil make about names at the start?
options: Most people are happy to change their names when they grow up
Names are less important today than in the past
Everyone should choose their own name at 18
They are closely linked to our identity, but we don't choose them
questions.why: He says our identity is linked to our name, yet it's usually given by our parents.

questions.q: Where does Bishop Anderson Jeremiah's first name come from?
options: His grandfather
A missionary who set up schools in South India
A famous Indian writer
A saint in the Bible who was known for his kindness
questions.why: He says it was the name of John Anderson, an educational missionary who set up schools in South India.

questions.q: How does Bishop Jeremiah feel about John Anderson?
options: He admires him completely
He has never heard much about him
He sees good aims, but also links to the colonial power
He thinks he was simply cruel and should be completely forgotten
questions.why: He says Anderson had very noble ambitions but was a big collaborator of the colonial establishment.

questions.q: Why did Bishop Jeremiah's grandparents become Christians?
options: To get free education abroad
Because the government forced them
To escape discrimination because of their low status
Because they married British missionaries who lived in the area
questions.why: Beth says low-status Indians, including his grandparents, escaped discrimination by converting.

questions.q: Where does Professor Robert Beckford's surname come from?
options: It was passed down from enslaved ancestors in Jamaica
It was the name of a Christian missionary who worked in Jamaica
It comes from a prophet in the Bible
He chose it himself as an adult
questions.why: Neil says Beckford is a slave name from his enslaved African ancestors in 18th-century Jamaica.

questions.q: Why did Professor Beckford name his son Micah?
options: It was his own father's name
It was the most popular name for baby boys that year
It sounds African and traditional
Micah was a prophet who challenged injustice
questions.why: He likes the idea of biblical figures who speak truth to power and challenge injustice.

questions.q: Why hasn't Professor Beckford given himself a new name?
options: His family asked him not to
He couldn't find one that felt right for him
He is proud of the name Beckford
It is far too difficult to change your name legally in Britain
questions.why: He says he could never find a name that really resonated with him.
